answers.core: It's just adding one signal. It seems far too small for an add-on.
answers.workaround:
I see two workarounds for this.

1) If I don't mind adding one extra frame of physics latency I can just treat the existing physics_frame signal as though it were the signal I wanted. I add objects to some kind of update datastructure in _physics_process, then when I see physics_frame I send that update. The issue here is now I'm sending updates that are already one tick old.

2) I could forget about utilizing _physics_process and just handle all of my networking in a function that responds to physics_frame. I would iterate through all the movable objects, decide which I want to include in my update, then send the update. I don't think this is quite as clean as what I'm proposing, but it should work and gets around the latency of 1.

title: Add a new signal to run after _physics_process, but before the physics step
